text:
Priya Nair: heads-up — woke up to a spike on /api/generate at ~02:10 UTC, but the follow-up postmortem flow felt messy again. want to propose a small project to tighten the after-action flow and rotation bot behavior.
Alex Gomez: thanks — agree. what's the main pain right now?
Priya Nair: multiple things: the incident-bot creates a thread, but it doesn't bake in the metadata we need for postmortems (customer list, affected routes, initial mitigation steps). then postmortems get created manually in a google doc and tracked in a spreadsheet by hand.
Jia Chen: real quick context: the oncall handoff last night had 3 different people pinged. nobody owned the postmortem until 10h later.
Marco Ruiz: yep — and action items often live in the doc with no assignee tags that our dashboards can pick up. follow-ups get missed.
Simon Blake: +1. We have the rotation bot but it only does paging and next-oncall mention. Could it be extended to automatically claim or nominate a postmortem owner based on severity? :thinking_face: 
incident-bot: [system] Alert created: INC-2026-0325-1843 - 5xx spike on /api/generate. Paging policy applied to eng-oncall.
Priya Nair: proposal sketch: 1) enrich incident-bot's initial payload with structured metadata (severity, estimated impacted customers, mitigation steps, candidate owners, time window). 2) auto-create a postmortem draft in our private docs space with that metadata filled in. 3) create canonical action items in a tracker (or JIRA) with owners and due dates from the start.
Alex Gomez: sounds solid. can we avoid putting sensitive customer identifiers into a public doc? needs to respect PII rules.
Jia Chen: doc privacy is a must. Maybe auto-create in a restricted folder and post a safe summary into the public thread. the draft doc can include a link that only allowed roles can open.
Marco Ruiz: how about the format of the postmortem doc? current template is long and free-form. suggest a compact "incident AAR" template focused on: timeline, impact, mitigation, root cause, action items, customer communication. One page summary up top.
Priya Nair: exactly. new template fields (proposal):
```
- Incident ID:
- Severity (S1/S2/S3):
- Start / End:
- Affected customers/services:
- Quick summary (1-2 lines):
- Timeline (bullet timestamps):
- Mitigation steps and who executed them:
- Root cause hypothesis:
- Action items (owner, due date, status):
- Post-incident customer comms needed: (yes/no) and owner
- Related runbooks / follow-ups:
```
Simon Blake: could postmortem-bot auto-parse action items from the doc and push them into our action-board? For example, when a new action line matches `- [ ] OwnerName: ... due 2026-04-01` it creates a task. :robot_face: 
postmortem-bot: [system] Example feature: detect TODOs in incident docs and push tasks to the action tracker.
Alex Gomez: yes — two things to ensure: 1) every action must have an owner and due date to be accepted, 2) tasks should carry a link back to the doc and the slack thread.
Jia Chen: also add an automatic 72-hour and 30-day reminders + ownership re-assign flow if no progress. we lose ownership after long tails.
Marco Ruiz: dashboard requirements (short): filter by team, severity, status (open/in-progress/closed), due date, and age. export to CSV. quick view of overdue items.
Priya Nair: rotation bot idea: when an S1/S2 is paged, the bot suggests a postmortem owner: primary oncall for the service OR the person who executed the mitigation. if nobody claims within 3h, escalate to service lead.
Simon Blake: do we have enough signal to pick "person who executed mitigation"? we might rely on the ack logs or runbook executions. incident-bot could capture ack events.
Priya Nair: yep, capture ack/command logs and include them in metadata.
Alex Gomez: what's the proposed command surface? i.e., how do we create the draft doc / tasks? Slash commands? reaction triggers?
Jia Chen: Options: `/incident create-draft` from the incident thread, or reaction `:pm-draft:` on the incident-bot message triggers creation. slash commands are clearer for audit.
Marco Ruiz: +1 for slash commands, but keep reactions as low-friction alternative. also, add an `edit` flow: `/pm edit INC-2026-0325-1843` opens an editable doc or posts the doc link in thread.
Priya Nair: lifecycle: incident ends -> incident-bot posts "incident ended" -> oncall runs `/incident create-draft` OR auto-create if severity >= S2. Draft created in restricted folder, postmortem-bot posts the link in-thread and creates tasks for listed action items.
Simon Blake: what about automation safety? don't want bot to create docs for small flaps. threshold toggle: auto-create only for severity >= S2 OR customer impact > X.
postmortem-bot: [system] Proposed metadata schema (example):
```
{
  "incident_id": "INC-2026-0325-1843",
  "severity": "S2",
  "start_ts": "2026-03-25T02:10:00Z",
  "end_ts": "2026-03-25T03:05:00Z",
  "affected_routes": "/api/generate",
  "estimated_customers": "<10 (paid)",
  "initial_mitigation": "rolled back v1.14.2 and scaled workers",
  "suggested_owner": "@alex.g",
  "notes": "ack logs show rapid restarts on model service"
}
```
Alex Gomez: looks good. implementation notes: keep schema small and stable; add a `flags` field for optional features (auto-create-doc, create-tasks).
Jia Chen: Ops checklist additions: add an explicit "PM notified? (Y/N)" field in doc; and a spot for customer impact helix (which customers to contact and recommended messaging).
Marco Ruiz: timeline integration: incident-bot should capture a compact timeline into the doc (auto-scrape messages that are formatted as `TIME - ACTION`). can surface the most relevant entries as highlights.
Priya Nair: next steps proposal: 1) RFC for schema + template, 2) small spike (2 weeks) to implement auto-create + task push for S2+, 3) dashboard prototype (sre/product metrics team) 4) pilot for one service (generate-api) for 4 weeks.
Simon Blake: resource ask? who can take the spike? I can do the bot changes, Jia can do doc/template, Marco can prototype the dashboard and Alex can own air-gap/security questions. Priya to coordinate.
Priya Nair: that distribution sounds great. I'll write the RFC draft and drop it in #eng-oncall-rfcs by EOD.
Alex Gomez: two blockers: 1) ensure docs API respects restricted folders and logs creation events, 2) we need JIRA/task-permissions to auto-assign. I'll sync with infra and platform.
Jia Chen: quick sample slash command UX: `/incident create-draft INC-2026-0325-1843 --auto-tasks true --private` -> replies with doc link and tasks created.
Marco Ruiz: and dashboard mock: small table + filter bar, each row links to doc + slack thread. + badge for overdue.
Simon Blake: can we also add a tiny mobile push notification to assigned owners for tasks due in 24h? many folks miss the slack nags.
Priya Nair: good idea. we should treat task reminders like oncall reminders: escalation chain + mobile/pager if needed for S1 actions.
postmortem-bot: [system] Created task example: INC-2026-0325-1843-1 - "Investigate model worker OOM" - owner: @jia.c - due: 2026-04-01 - status: open.
Alex Gomez: ok let's keep momentum — Priya, tag me on RFC. I'll book a 30m sync next week to unblock infra permissions.
Priya Nair: will do. Thanks everyone. I'll follow up with proposed RFC link here when ready. :sparkles:
Marco Ruiz: thanks, excited to reduce the friction. small automation wins will help.
Simon Blake: thanks — evening for me, will review RFC tomorrow. :wave:
